text: Once their jaw tenses, that's their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. If they're drinking a lot of plain water, even a single normal dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so I'd have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty. A headache that gets worse and worse is how low sodium tends to show up, often with throwing up or confusion, and it's time to call medics. The same goes for muscles getting weaker and weaker, or palpitations where the heart skips beats, which can mean their potassium is low. And a seizure or collapse means the MDMA toxicity has become an emergency, so get medics there right away.

marked.s: Muscle weakness or palpitations, where the heart pounds or skips, can mean their potassium is low instead, like my second wife's, and that needs help too.
And if they have a seizure or collapse, which overheating or MDMA toxicity can also cause, that raises it to an emergency: call medics right away.
When their jaw tenses, that's also the time to stop taking MDMA and get them to slow down and cool off.
Keep watching them: a headache that keeps getting worse can mean their sodium is getting too low, and so can confusion or vomiting.
Weakness or palpitations can mean their potassium is dropping.
A seizure or a collapse raises the stakes, so call medics, since overheating and MDMA toxicity can cause those too.
None of the volunteers whose drinking was limited did, so keep water to small sips.
